name: CLIPPERS
aliases: chronic lymphocytic inflammation with pontine perivascular enhancement responsive to steroids

reference.source: Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
clinicalPearls: A chronic inflammatory disorder centred on the pons and hindbrain, presenting with subacute ataxia, diplopia, dysarthria, and sensory disturbance
The hallmark MRI finding is punctate and curvilinear ('salt-and-pepper' or peppering) gadolinium enhancement concentrated in the pons and cerebellum
Pathology shows perivascular lymphocytic (predominantly T-cell) infiltration without a defined alternative cause
By definition the disorder is markedly and rapidly responsive to corticosteroids, and relapse on withdrawal is characteristic
It is a diagnosis of exclusion, requiring careful search for lymphoma, vasculitis, sarcoidosis, and infection
Large or tumefactive enhancement, necrosis, or atypical features should prompt biopsy and reconsideration of the diagnosis
Long-term steroid-sparing immunosuppression is usually required to prevent relapse and progressive disability
reference.pathophysiology: CLIPPERS is characterised by a chronic, predominantly T-lymphocytic perivascular inflammatory infiltrate concentrated in the pons, brainstem, and cerebellum, with variable extension along white-matter tracts. The inflammation surrounds small vessels and correlates with the punctate perivascular contrast enhancement seen on MRI. No specific antigen or antibody has been identified, and the disorder is defined clinically, radiologically, and pathologically together with its striking corticosteroid responsiveness. Because similar perivascular inflammation can herald lymphoma or other conditions, CLIPPERS is regarded as a syndrome requiring exclusion of mimics and ongoing surveillance.
additionalDifferentials: Primary or secondary central nervous system vasculitis
additionalInvestigations: MRI of the brain with contrast to demonstrate the characteristic punctate pontine and cerebellar enhancement
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis including cytology and flow cytometry to exclude lymphoma
Serum and CSF markers for sarcoidosis, vasculitis, and infection
Whole-body imaging to search for occult lymphoma or systemic inflammatory disease
Brain biopsy in atypical, tumefactive, or steroid-unresponsive cases
Serial MRI to monitor response and detect emerging lymphoma
redFlags: Large, tumefactive, or necrotic lesions atypical for CLIPPERS
Poor or incomplete response to corticosteroids
Progressive brainstem dysfunction with bulbar or respiratory compromise
Emergence of features suggesting lymphoma on follow-up
reference.prognosis: With corticosteroids and maintenance immunosuppression most patients improve and stabilise, but delayed treatment or repeated relapses can lead to pontine atrophy and fixed disability; vigilance for evolving lymphoma is essential.
pitfalls: Diagnosing CLIPPERS without adequately excluding lymphoma and other mimics
Withdrawing corticosteroids without steroid-sparing cover and precipitating relapse
Ignoring atypical imaging features that warrant biopsy
Failing to arrange long-term radiological surveillance
references: Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology
management: Corticosteroid therapy is the mainstay, producing marked and rapid clinical and radiological improvement that also helps confirm the diagnosis.
Long-term steroid-sparing immunosuppression such as methotrexate, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil or rituximab to maintain remission and limit steroid toxicity.
Gradual steroid tapering under maintenance therapy, because relapse on withdrawal is typical.
Diagnostic brain biopsy in atypical, tumefactive or steroid-unresponsive cases to exclude lymphoma, vasculitis and sarcoidosis.
Serial MRI and clinical review to monitor response and detect emerging lymphoma.
Rehabilitation and symptomatic support for ataxia, diplopia, dysarthria and sensory disturbance.
Neurology or neuroimmunology specialist follow-up to guard against fixed disability from pontine atrophy.
